newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Usinor Sacilor CEO sees steel prices up.
newsitem.headline: Usinor Sacilor CEO sees steel prices up.

text.p: Francis Mer, head of French steel group Usinor Sacilor and head of European industry body Eurofer, said on Friday that steel volume was rising in 1997 and hoped prices would follow.

"(1997) has started well in volume terms. Imports remain weak, because prices remain weak in Europe, even if slight improvements can be seen and should accelerate in the spring," Mer told Belgian newspaper L'Echo in an interview.
Eurofer estimated total European steel market tonnages would return to 1995's level of around 150 million tonnes after falling to around 130 million tonnes in 1996.
"We foresee a much better economic situation in 1997, which should allow us to, at least, return to the level of real consumption of 1995," Mer said.
1996 was characterised by de-stocking by customers, lower imports from eastern Europe due to lower prices within the European Union (EU), and higher exports.
The positive balance of exports to imports reached 16 million tonnes, up from six million tonnes in 1995. "This eased the impact...of the fall in deliveries in Europe," he said.
